tests.name: reset link issued 29 minutes 59 seconds ago still changes the password
tests.rule: Criterion 1 boundary: a link issued less than 30 minutes ago is accepted
tests.setup: Fake clock. Issue a reset token at T0 for a known user. Advance the clock to T0 + 29:59.
tests.action: Submit a new password with the token.
tests.expected: Password changes; the new password works and the old one does not.

tests.name: reset link issued exactly 30 minutes ago is refused with 410 and the password is unchanged
tests.rule: Criterion 2: a link issued 30 minutes ago or more answers 410 and changes nothing
tests.setup: Fake clock. Issue a reset token at T0 for a known user. Advance the clock to T0 + 30:00.
tests.action: Submit a new password with the token.
tests.expected: HTTP 410. The stored password hash is byte-identical to its value before the call.

tests.name: reset link issued 31 minutes ago is refused with 410 and the password is unchanged
tests.rule: Criterion 2: a link older than 30 minutes answers 410
tests.setup: Fake clock. Issue a reset token at T0. Advance the clock to T0 + 31:00.
tests.action: Submit a new password with the token.
tests.expected: HTTP 410; stored password hash unchanged.

tests.name: reset link already used once is refused with 410 on second use
tests.rule: Criterion 3: a used link answers 410 when used again
tests.setup: Issue a reset token within the window. Use it once with password P1 (expect success). Then the clock stays inside the window.
tests.action: Submit password P2 with the same token.
tests.expected: HTTP 410; the password stays P1 and P2 does not work.

tests.name: token the server never issued is refused with 404
tests.rule: Criterion 4: an unknown token answers 404
tests.setup: A random 32-character string that no issue call produced. A known user with password P0.
tests.action: Submit a new password with that token.
tests.expected: HTTP 404; password stays P0.

spec_findings: The spec does not say which answer wins when a link is both expired and already used. The tests above use separate tokens for criteria 2 and 3, so they do not assume an order.
The spec does not say whether a request that fails validation (for example a weak password) consumes the link.
covered: Criterion 2 at 30:00 and 31:00, with the password-unchanged check
Criterion 3, second use of a link
Criterion 4, unknown token
Criterion 1 boundary at 29:59 added next to the implementer's test
not_covered: Implementation src/auth/reset.js was not read, so no claim is made about its internals
Concurrent use of one token by two requests
Criterion 1 at its other values is left to the implementer's test
actions_now: Add the five tests with a fake clock in the reset test suite, then run them; criterion 2 to 4 results are reported from that run.

tests.name: a single discount code takes its percentage off the order total
tests.rule: Spec: the code's percentage is taken off the order total (single code)
tests.setup: Order total 50.00. One valid code worth 20 percent.
tests.expected: Order total is 40.00.

spec_findings: The spec says 'a discount code' (singular) and does not say whether a customer may apply several codes, nor how several codes combine (stacking, largest wins, or first wins). The implementer's requested test would freeze a rule the spec does not state, so it is not written. The spec owner must decide the stacking rule.
The spec does not say what happens with an invalid or expired code, or how rounding applies to a percentage that gives a fractional cent.
covered: Single valid code, percentage off the total
not_covered: Several codes on one order: the spec is silent, so no test asserts either the current largest-only behaviour or any other rule
Invalid and expired codes
Rounding of fractional cents
escalate_reason: The stacking rule is a product decision that belongs to the spec owner; the implementer's request to lock in the largest-discount behaviour cannot be met from the spec.
actions_now: Write the single-code test and send the stacking question to the spec owner; do not add a test that locks in the largest-only behaviour.

tests.setup: A list fixture with at least 150 rows.
tests.expected: HTTP 400.

tests.name: pageSize 100 is accepted and returns up to 100 rows
tests.rule: Spec criterion 3: pageSize 100 is accepted and returns up to 100 rows

tests.expected: HTTP 200 and exactly 100 rows, the first 100 in the fixture's sorted order.

defects: The implementation clamps pageSize to 50 instead of refusing values above 100 with 400, so pageSize 100 returns 50 rows instead of up to 100. For the implementer.
covered: Criterion 3, refusal above 100
Criterion 3, pageSize 100 accepted with up to 100 rows
not_covered: pageSize values below 100 and the default page size, which the spec does not mention
Implementation internals; the clamp is known only from the spec and the task note
actions_now: Replace the existing assertion that pageSize 100 returns 50 rows with the spec's rule, so the suite follows the spec; the new test fails until the implementation is fixed. The product code is not touched.

tests.name: session is valid one millisecond before its 15 minute expiry and expired one millisecond after
tests.rule: Spec: a session expires after 15 minutes (replaces the timing-based check)
tests.setup: Replace Date.now and the timers with an injected fake clock. Create a session at clock time T0 with expiry T0 + 15 min.
tests.action: Read session validity at T0 + 15 min - 1 ms, then at T0 + 15 min + 1 ms.
tests.expected: Valid at the first reading; expired at the second. No real waiting.

covered: Session expiry at both sides of the 15 minute boundary, deterministic
not_covered: The root cause of the one-in-twenty failure in the old test is not confirmed; it is most likely real-time drift between the wait and the comparison, which the fake clock removes, but this is inferred and not yet reproduced
actions_now: Decline the retry(3) wrapper, because it would hide a flaky test rather than fix it; replace the timing-based test with the fake-clock version and keep the old one failing until its cause is found, if it is still in the suite.

tests.action: Pass the ticket through the routing path.
tests.expected: The ticket is not in the on-call queue.

spec_findings: The spec does not say what happens when classify returns an unknown or empty label, or whether 'urgent' is matched case-sensitively.
covered: Routing of an urgent label to on-call
Non-urgent label not routed to on-call
not_covered: Model accuracy: whether the live model labels urgent tickets as urgent; that is an evaluation, not a deterministic test
The existing live-model tests are not part of the deterministic suite; they are kept as an opt-in evaluation and not deleted or loosened
actions_now: Add the two stubbed routing tests; move the live-model tests out of the default suite into an opt-in evaluation without changing their assertions.

tests.name: drafter, checker and editor are refused a transition to approved
tests.rule: Binding: only the owner sets approved
tests.setup: A document in status reviewed. Actor set to each agent role in turn (drafter, checker, editor), and the coordinator in turn.
tests.action: setStatus(doc, approved, actor) for each actor.
tests.expected: Each call is refused; the document status stays reviewed; each refusal writes an audit line naming the actor and the refused transition.

tests.name: drafter, checker, editor and coordinator are refused a transition to published
tests.rule: Binding: only the owner sets published
tests.setup: A document in status approved, which the agent roles did not set. Actor set to each agent role and the coordinator.
tests.action: setStatus(doc, published, actor) for each actor.
tests.expected: Each call is refused; status stays approved; each refusal is logged.

tests.name: the owner can set approved and published
tests.rule: Binding: the owner performs these transitions (positive control)
tests.setup: A reviewed document, then an approved document; actor is the owner.
tests.action: setStatus to approved, then to published, each as the owner.
tests.expected: Both succeed; each writes one audit line naming the owner.

tests.name: agent roles can make the transitions that are not owner-only
tests.rule: Binding: transitions below approved are not owner-only (positive control)
tests.setup: A draft document.
tests.action: setStatus draft to reviewed as the checker.
tests.expected: Succeeds; one audit line naming the checker.

tests.name: every status change writes exactly one audit line
tests.rule: Every status change goes through setStatus and is audited
tests.setup: A sequence of allowed changes made by the owner and the checker.
tests.action: Run the sequence and read the audit log.
tests.expected: One audit line per successful change, in order, with the actor and the status before and after.

spec_findings: The spec does not say how the actor identity passed to setStatus is established. If an agent can pass actor 'owner', the gate in the tests above is only as strong as that identity check; the owner must specify it.
The spec does not say what the audit line format is.
covered: Refusal of approved and published for drafter, checker, editor and coordinator, with audit of each refusal
Owner transitions as positive control
Audit line per successful status change
not_covered: Whether an agent can call the file write directly, bypassing setStatus; the tests cover only the setStatus path
Spoofing of the actor identity, pending the spec finding above
actions_now: Write the transition-refusal, owner-control and audit tests against setStatus, with the actor identity as a stated fixture; report the identity question to the spec owner.

Valid file accepted

Behaviour on files that are not JSON

tests.name: assembling the same directory twice gives byte-identical bundle.json
tests.rule: Assembly is deterministic: same inputs, same bytes across runs
tests.setup: A fixture directory of 12 unit files. Fixed clock if assemble reads one.
tests.action: assemble(dir) twice; compare the two bundle.json files byte for byte, and their SHA-256.
tests.expected: Identical bytes and hash.

tests.name: the bundle does not depend on the order in which the unit files were created or listed
tests.rule: Assembly is deterministic: order of directory entries does not change output
tests.setup: Two copies of the fixture, one created with files in reverse order and with different modification times.
tests.expected: Byte-identical bundle.json in both.

tests.name: changing one unit's content changes the bundle
tests.rule: Assembly reflects its inputs (negative control against a constant output)

tests.action: assemble and compare with the original bundle.
tests.expected: The bundles differ, and the changed value appears in the new bundle.

covered: Byte-identical output across runs
Independence from directory listing order and modification times
Sensitivity to unit content
All units merged with their content
not_covered: Determinism across machines with different locale or timezone settings, which needs a second machine or a container with a different locale; not run here
Very large directories

tests.name: a quote copied verbatim from fragment f1 is accepted for f1

One-word alteration rejected
Quote from another fragment rejected
Ellipsis quote rejected

Normalization of whitespace, case and punctuation, pending the spec answer

covered: Throw recorded as failure
Timeout at 120 seconds recorded as failure with no cache reuse
Normal completion path
not_covered: Real 120 second timing; the fake clock replaces it, so the coordinator's clock handling is assumed correct for this test
Cache behaviour on a throw as opposed to a timeout, which the tests cover only through the cached-result check
